subject: sst
prompt_en: A child says: 'Our city is dirty because the municipality is lazy. We don't need to do anything.' What is missing in this thinking?
prompt_hi: Ek bachcha kehta hai: 'Hamara sheher gandaa hai kyunki nagar nigam aalsi hai. Humein kuch karne ki zaroorat nahi.' Is soch mein kya kami hai?
answer: Citizens share the responsibility: not littering, separating wet and dry waste, paying taxes and reporting problems; the municipality and citizens together keep a city clean.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if every home in a colony starts separating wet and dry waste, what changes for the municipality and the city?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar colony ka har ghar geela aur sookha kachra alag karne lage, to nagar nigam aur sheher ke liye kya badlega?
answer: Waste is easier to collect and process: wet waste can become compost, dry waste can be recycled, less goes to landfills, and streets stay cleaner.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Draw (or describe) an organisation chart of a municipal corporation: people, wards, councillors, mayor, commissioner, departments.
prompt_hi: Municipal corporation ka organisation chart banao (ya batao): log, wards, councillors, mayor, commissioner, departments.
answer: People of each ward elect councillors → councillors form the council headed by the mayor and make decisions → the commissioner (appointed) runs departments like water, sanitation and roads that carry them out.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare a gram panchayat and a municipal corporation: what is similar and what is different?
prompt_hi: Gram panchayat aur municipal corporation ko compare karo: kya milta-julta hai aur kya alag?
answer: Similar: both are elected local governments that handle local needs like water, roads, cleanliness and lights. Different: the panchayat serves villages, with a sarpanch and the gram sabha of all adults; the corporation serves big cities, with wards, councillors, a mayor and an appointed commissioner.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find out (or guess) which urban local body or panchayat looks after your area. Name one service it gives you and one thing your family does to help it work.
prompt_hi: Pata karo (ya andaza lagao) ki tumhare ilaake ko kaunsa local body dekhta hai. Ek service batao jo woh deta hai aur ek cheez jo tumhara parivaar uski madad ke liye karta hai.
answer: Any correct local body (municipal corporation, council, nagar panchayat or gram panchayat), one real service (water, garbage pickup, streetlights) and one citizen action (separating waste, paying tax, reporting a broken light).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend how a city is governed and how citizens can make it work better.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko sikhao ki sheher ka shasan kaise chalta hai aur naagrik use behtar kaise bana sakte hain.
answer: The city is divided into wards that elect councillors; the council is headed by the mayor; an appointed commissioner runs departments; the body provides water, garbage collection, lights, roads and more, paid for by taxes and grants; citizens vote, pay taxes, report problems, attend ward meetings and do their part like separating waste.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What is the main difference between economic and non-economic activities?
prompt_hi: Economic aur non-economic activities mein mukhya farq kya hai?
answer: Economic activities are done for payment (money or in kind) or to earn; non-economic activities are done without payment, out of love, care, duty or service.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare Meena cooking dinner for her family with Meena cooking in a restaurant kitchen. Which is economic, and why?
prompt_hi: Meena ka parivaar ke liye khana banana aur Meena ka restaurant ki kitchen mein khana banana compare karo. Kaunsa economic hai aur kyon?
answer: Cooking in the restaurant is economic because she is paid for it; cooking for her family is non-economic because it is done out of care, without payment — the activity is the same, the purpose differs.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do we say unpaid household work is valuable even though no one is paid for it?
prompt_hi: Hum kyon kehte hain ki bina paise ka gharelu kaam keemti hai, jabki iske liye koi paise nahi milte?
answer: Because families could not function without it — meals, cleanliness and care keep everyone healthy and able to study or work; if someone else were paid to do it, it would cost a lot.

subject: sst
prompt_en: List all the work done in your home in one day and mark each task as paid or unpaid. How many are unpaid?
prompt_hi: Apne ghar mein ek din mein hone wale saare kaam list karo aur har kaam pe paid ya unpaid likho. Kitne unpaid hain?
answer: Any honest list; usually most home tasks (cooking, cleaning, washing, caring, shopping for the family) are unpaid non-economic work, showing how much unpaid work families rely on.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A student says: 'Teaching is always an economic activity.' Give an example that shows this is wrong.
prompt_hi: Ek student kehta hai: 'Padhana hamesha economic activity hai.' Ek example do jo dikhaaye ki yeh galat hai.
answer: A parent teaching their own child at home, or a volunteer teaching children for free, is non-economic — no payment, done out of care or service.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A farm worker is paid in sacks of rice instead of money. Is this economic work? Explain.
prompt_hi: Ek khet mazdoor ko paison ki jagah chawal ki boriyan milti hain. Kya yeh economic kaam hai? Samjhao.
answer: Yes — payment in kind (rice) is still payment for work, so it is an economic activity.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if all the farmers in India stopped working for a month, who else would be affected and how?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar Bharat ke saare kisaan ek mahine kaam band kar dein, to aur kaun prabhavit hoga aur kaise?
answer: Almost everyone: food would run short and prices rise; mills, shops, transporters and restaurants that depend on crops would lose work — showing how all work is connected.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why should we respect a sanitation worker's job as much as any other job?
prompt_hi: Hamein safai karmachari ke kaam ki izzat utni hi kyon karni chahiye jitni kisi aur kaam ki?
answer: Their work keeps cities clean and protects everyone's health; all honest work is needed and has dignity.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Make a two-column table (economic / non-economic) for: a doctor in a clinic, a doctor treating her own mother, a tailor stitching for customers, a girl stitching a gift for a friend.
prompt_hi: Do column ki table banao (economic / non-economic): clinic mein doctor, apni maa ka ilaaj karti doctor, grahakon ke liye silai karta darzi, dost ke liye tohfa silti ladki.
answer: Economic: doctor in a clinic, tailor stitching for customers. Non-economic: doctor treating her own mother, girl stitching a gift.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Give two examples of non-economic activities that help the community.
prompt_hi: Do aise non-economic activities ke examples do jo samudaay ki madad karti hain.
answer: Any two: volunteering in a clean-up drive, helping at a community kitchen, teaching neighbours' children for free, blood donation, helping flood victims.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a younger sibling the difference between economic and non-economic work and why all work matters.
prompt_hi: Chhote bhai ya behen ko economic aur non-economic kaam ka farq sikhao aur batao ki har kaam kyon zaroori hai.
answer: Economic work is done for payment (money or in kind); non-economic work is done out of love, care, duty or service; the same action can be either depending on purpose; unpaid home work is real and valuable; all honest work has dignity and we depend on each other.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Give one example each of primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
prompt_hi: Primary, secondary aur tertiary activities ka ek-ek example do.
answer: Any correct examples, e.g., primary: farming, fishing, mining; secondary: sugar mill, textile mill, furniture making; tertiary: transport, teaching, shopkeeping, banking.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Turn this into a chain with labels: cotton grows on a farm → yarn and cloth are made in a mill → a truck carries it → a shop sells it. Label each step's sector.
prompt_hi: Ise labels ke saath chain mein badlo: khet mein kapaas ugti hai → mill mein dhaaga aur kapda banta hai → truck le jaata hai → dukaan bechti hai. Har step ka sector likho.
answer: Farm — primary; mill — secondary; truck (transport) — tertiary; shop (trade) — tertiary.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A student writes: 'Mining is a secondary activity because miners use big machines.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Ek student ne likha: 'Mining secondary activity hai kyunki miners badi machines use karte hain.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Mining is primary because it takes minerals directly from nature; using machines does not change the sector.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if sugarcane farmers have a very bad harvest, what will happen to sugar mills, sweet shops and sugar prices?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar ganne ke kisaanon ki fasal bahut kharab ho, to sugar mills, mithai ki dukaanon aur cheeni ke daam ka kya hoga?
answer: Mills get less cane and make less sugar, sweet shops get less or costlier sugar, and sugar prices are likely to rise — sectors depend on each other.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Trace a loaf of bread through the three sectors.
prompt_hi: Ek bread ke packet ko teeno sectors se hokar trace karo.
answer: Wheat grown by a farmer (primary) → milled into flour and baked into bread in a bakery (secondary) → transported and sold in a shop (tertiary).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do we say the three sectors depend on each other? Give one example.
prompt_hi: Hum kyon kehte hain ki teeno sectors ek-doosre pe nirbhar hain? Ek example do.
answer: Each needs the others: mills need raw materials from farms and mines, farmers need tools and fertiliser from factories and transport and markets to sell crops, and services need goods to move and sell — e.g., a textile mill needs cotton from farmers and trucks to deliver cloth.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare a fishing village on the coast with an industrial town: which sector is likely to employ more people in each, and why?
prompt_hi: Samudra kinare ke machhuaaron ke gaon aur ek audyogik sheher ko compare karo: har jagah kaunsa sector zyada logon ko kaam deta hoga, aur kyon?
answer: Fishing village: the primary sector (fishing) because the sea is its main resource; industrial town: the secondary sector (factories), with tertiary services in both.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Classify: (a) a carpenter making a table (b) a dairy farmer milking cows (c) a doctor (d) a construction worker building a house.
prompt_hi: Classify karo: (a) mez banata badhai (b) gaay doodhne wala dairy kisaan (c) doctor (d) ghar banane wala construction worker.
answer: (a) secondary, (b) primary, (c) tertiary, (d) secondary.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Walk around your neighbourhood (or think of it). Name one primary, one secondary and one tertiary activity you can find there.
prompt_hi: Apne mohalle mein ghoomo (ya socho). Wahan ek primary, ek secondary aur ek tertiary activity batao.
answer: Any correctly classified local examples, e.g., primary: vegetable farming, dairy; secondary: flour chakki, tailoring unit, sweet-making; tertiary: shops, autos, school, bank, clinic.

subject: sst
prompt_en: In one sentence each, define primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
prompt_hi: Ek-ek vaakya mein primary, secondary aur tertiary activities ki paribhasha do.
answer: Primary: taking things directly from nature; secondary: turning raw materials into goods; tertiary: providing services.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend the three sectors of the economy using the journey of a cotton shirt.
prompt_hi: Ek cotton shirt ke safar ke zariye dost ko economy ke 3 sectors sikhao.
answer: Cotton is grown by farmers (primary: from nature) → spun, woven and stitched in mills and units (secondary: making goods) → transported, advertised and sold in shops (tertiary: services); each sector depends on the others.

subject: english
prompt_en: Read: 'Every evening, Meenu sat by the river while her brothers did homework. "Why can't I go to school too?" she asked. The river seemed to whisper, "Keep asking. Every question is a small step." Next morning, Meenu walked to the headmaster's door.' Why do you think Meenu asked the river her question, and not her family?
prompt_hi: Socho — Meenu ne apna sawaal ghar walon se kyun nahi, nadi se poocha?
answer: She felt no one at home would listen or say yes, so she shared her feelings with the river, which felt like a safe friend

subject: english
prompt_en: Read: 'Every evening, Meenu sat by the river while her brothers did homework. "Why can't I go to school too?" she asked. The river seemed to whisper, "Keep asking. Every question is a small step." Next morning, Meenu walked to the headmaster's door.' What do you think Meenu will say to the headmaster?
prompt_hi: Agla kya hoga? Headmaster ke darwaaze par Meenu kya bolegi?
answer: She will ask if she can join the school and learn to read

subject: english
prompt_en: Make a question beginning with 'Why' from this sentence: 'The river flows to the sea.'
prompt_hi: Is sentence se 'Why' wala sawaal banao: 'The river flows to the sea.'
answer: Why does the river flow to the sea?

subject: english
prompt_en: Find the mistake and say it correctly: 'Why you are sad, Meenu?'
prompt_hi: Is sawaal mein galti dhoondho: 'Why you are sad, Meenu?'
answer: Why are you sad, Meenu?

subject: english
prompt_en: Listen to two sentences: 'Where does the river go?' and 'Where the river goes is a mystery.' Which one is a question, and how do you know?
prompt_hi: Do sentences hain. Kaunsa sawaal hai, aur kaise pata chala?
answer: 'Where does the river go?' is the question, because 'does' comes before the subject 'the river'

subject: english
prompt_en: Ask a question about time from this sentence, starting with 'When': 'The school bell rings at nine.'
prompt_hi: Ab 'When' se sawaal banao: 'The school bell rings at nine.'
answer: When does the school bell ring?

subject: english
prompt_en: 'The river seemed to whisper, Keep asking.' What does 'whisper' mean here: shout loudly, speak very softly, or run fast?
prompt_hi: 'Whisper' ka matlab kya hai yahaan? Zor se chillana, bahut dheere bolna, ya tez bhaagna?
answer: Speak very softly

subject: english
prompt_en: Say this in English using the word 'eager': 'Meenu ko padhne ki bahut ichchha thi.'
prompt_hi: Is Hindi line ko English mein bolo, 'eager' word use karke: 'Meenu ko padhne ki bahut ichchha thi.'
answer: Meenu was eager to study.

subject: english
prompt_en: 'Curious' is an adjective. Fill the blank with its noun: 'Her ___ made her ask many questions.'
prompt_hi: 'Curious' ka naam-shabd (noun) kya hoga? 'Her ___ made her ask many questions.'
answer: curiosity

subject: english
prompt_en: In the story, the river says, 'Every question is a small step.' What does the writer want us to understand from this?
prompt_hi: Nadi kehti hai 'Every question is a small step.' Lekhak hume kya samjhana chahte hain?
answer: Asking questions is how learning begins, so we should not be afraid to ask

subject: english
prompt_en: Your little cousin asks, 'Why is the story of the girl and the river important?' Explain its big message to her in two or three sentences.
prompt_hi: Chhoti cousin ko samjhao — nadi aur ladki wali kahani ka asli sandesh kya hai? Do-teen line mein.
answer: The girl wants to learn but is kept at home; by asking questions and speaking up she finds her way to school, so every child, girls too, deserves to learn and should keep asking

subject: english
prompt_en: In 'The rope was high, my arms were sore, / I fell, I rose, I tried once more,' which two words rhyme?
prompt_hi: In lines mein kaunse do words rhyme karte hain?
answer: sore and more
